summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase and execute-phase workflows end-to-end for Phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) in the cipher-box repo, including research, planning, wave-based execution, and — after the initial verification found the desync bug unfixed — a full gap-closure cycle.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 was fully planned (12 plans/7 waves) and executed, with a scope decision (D-07 full boundary) locked mid-flow; the initial phase verifier found the SC#5 desync bug unfixed (4/5 must-haves), triggering a 2-plan gap-closure cycle (waves 8-9) that added a gated `forceResolve` live re-resolve path; the desync e2e now passes and the re-verifier confirmed the fix code-side, landing the phase in `human_needed` status pending an independent e2e re-run. A second, independent git worktree for Phase 69 was also created off origin/main but not yet driven.

repo: gsd-tools's `query commit` helper frequently reports `commit_failed` even when the commit landed cleanly — always verify with `git log` before trusting the error (recurring across this session, consistent with existing memory).

Executor subagents in this GSD setup tend to prematurely mark requirement checkboxes `[x]` in REQUIREMENTS.md before all of a requirement's acceptance criteria (e.g. deletion of old services) are actually met — the orchestrator must spot-check and revert these until the true completing plan lands.

Worktree `baseRef` config can be `head` vs `fresh`(origin/main) — for a pnpm monorepo with many single-plan waves, worktree-per-plan execution is overhead (needs its own `pnpm install`); sequential execution on the main tree was chosen instead and worked fine since same-wave plans were kept file-disjoint by the planner.
The advisory `gap-analysis.plan-post` gate's JSON `rendered` field can contain control characters that break naive parsing — run the underlying check command directly instead.
zsh glob syntax broke a grep command used to map deletion-blocking importers; had to redo it with corrected syntax.

code.finding: Plan 68.2-01 wired the ROT-07 `enforceResolved` anti-rollback gate onto the root resolve path (previously ungated).
Plan 68.2-01 also gated `dfsFindFolder`'s child-loop resolve with `enforceResolved`, closing the read-path zero-gating gap identified in RESEARCH Pitfall 2.
Pre-existing write-path ROT-07 gate location, used as the reference pattern for the two new read-path gate sites.

`ensureFolderLoaded` short-circuits on cached `folderTree` entries and never re-resolves IPNS on repeat navigation — root cause of the SC#5 desync bug (owner can't see grantee's upload without writing first).
Gap-closure plan 68.2-13's `doReresolveFolderInPlace` fails closed before any floor mutation, mirroring the original gate's fail-closed ordering.
Gap-closure re-resolve path routes through `enforceResolved` just like the original read-path gate, preserving the security invariant.
In-flight dedup logic (`reresolveFolderInPlace`) added by plan 68.2-13 to prevent redundant concurrent re-resolves.

`resolveChildren`'s docstring justifies skipping unverifiable siblings on per-child resolve failure as safe: the target folder is already gated via `ensureFolderLoaded`/`dfsFindFolder` before this runs, so no stale/attacker content is ever rendered — an availability tradeoff, not a security regression.

workflow: When an executor subagent reports a deviation on security-adjacent code (e.g. widening error handling on a read path), read the actual implementation and independently re-run the security-relevant tests rather than trusting the self-report — caught that a graceful degradation change did not swallow the ROT-07 gate.

Before pausing/resuming execution with a scheduled wakeup, always fetch the *current* wall-clock time right before computing the delay — computing it off a stale timestamp (from before a quota interruption) caused a wakeup scheduled ~25 minutes later than intended.

For multi-wave phase execution, spot-checking every wave (commits, SUMMARY, targeted + independent test re-runs) before advancing catches issues (premature checkbox marks, coverage claims) that a pure pass/fail read of the executor's report would miss.

When a planner's file-scoped plans don't cover every consumer of code being deleted, expect executors to surface unowned residual importers wave-by-wave; re-grep for the true residual immediately before the deletion plan rather than trusting the plan's original file list.

friction: `git fetch` failed from the sandboxed session (no network access to GitHub) when creating the Phase 69 worktree; had to rely on the last-known local `origin/main` ref, verified as current by cross-checking against the 68.2 branch's fork point.
Hit the session's usage-limit/quota mid-execution (reset at 4am Europe/Berlin), interrupting the pause/resume flow.

First `ScheduleWakeup` call used a `delaySeconds` computed off a pre-quota-gap timestamp, resulting in a wakeup scheduled ~25 minutes late (04:35 instead of 04:10); had to recompute against the real current time and reschedule.
Could not cleanly retract/cancel the now-unneeded scheduled wakeup after the user said to skip it and just keep going — had to rely on it being a harmless no-op when it eventually fired.
gap-analysis.plan-post gate's JSON output had control characters that broke the initial parse, requiring a direct re-run of the underlying check.
A zsh grep/glob command for mapping deletion-blocking importers had invalid syntax and needed to be redone.
open_items: Phase 68.2 verifier returned `human_needed`: the SC#5 fix (code, tests, and one desync-spec run) is confirmed, but an independent/CI re-run of the full web-e2e suite in a live stack is still needed since the verifier couldn't re-run it after plan 14 tore the stack down; a UAT item was logged for this.

13 pre-existing web-e2e failures remain after the gap fix, several already tracked as pre-existing Phase 68.1 gaps (GAP-1 AEAD, GAP-2 cold-reload DFS) rather than caused by this phase — not yet triaged/fixed.

Phase 69 worktree (`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box-phase69`, branch `feat/phase-69-fuse-winfsp`) was created off origin/main but the user has not yet started `/gsd-discuss-phase 69` in it; still fully pending.
Optional follow-up offered but not yet executed: copying Phase 68.2's CONTEXT.md/RESEARCH.md into the Phase 69 worktree as reference material for its design-mirroring dependency.
